name: MO-08
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+27 district partisanship in rural Missouri
Incumbent advantage with no polling or outside spending to shift the race
model.rationale: The R+27 lean, Smith's overwhelming financial edge, and a 96% market price leave no credible path for Reichard, who has raised under $6,000. Nothing in the evidence moves the race away from a deep-Republican baseline.
model.watch: Only a dramatic, unforeseen scandal or late outside spending blitz against Smith would put this on the board.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
MO-08 is one of the most Republican-leaning House districts in the country, with a partisan lean of R+27. Incumbent Jason Smith is running for reelection with a massive financial advantage: more than $5 million raised and $5 million on hand, against a Democratic challenger who has raised under $6,000. A Libertarian is also on the ballot, but with negligible resources.

No public polls, expert ratings, or outside spending exist for this race, and prediction markets give Smith roughly a 96% chance of winning. The forecast rests entirely on fundamentals, which point to a comfortable Smith victory in the low-twenties margin range.
